name: Team Capacity Heatmap
note: Each cell's load ÷ capacity is a registered @property number fed through a two-stage color-mix(in oklch) ramp (empty → healthy → overbooked), so cells sweep in on mount via @starting-style with a diagonal stagger and glide to their new colour when you move an assignment to a teammate; rows are subgrid tracks that re-sort with a WAAPI FLIP, and a second view stacks the same assignments into demand vs capacity bars. name: OKR Roll-up Tree
note: Key-result progress is (now − start) ÷ (target − start), so lower-is-better targets need no special case, and every objective is the mean of its children; rings are a registered <number> driving a conic-gradient with the percentage counted up by an @property <integer> through a CSS counter. Logging a check-in sends a pulse up the tree edges (WAAPI stroke-dashoffset) and each ancestor re-rings as it arrives; the layout springs between a horizontal tidy tree and an indented outline by container width. Set --dbp-okr-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Release Go / No-Go Desk
note: Readiness is cleared weight ÷ total weight (required items count 1, optional 0.5), drawn as a six-gate SVG dial whose arcs fill by transitioning stroke-dasharray on pathLength=100 paths; failing metrics can be re-measured or waived with a recorded reason, owners can only sign a clear gate, and GO unlocks the approval stamp. The countdown is a fixed snapshot plus real elapsed seconds on an interval that pauses off screen (IntersectionObserver) and in hidden tabs, and the history view plots the live score against the two previous releases. name: Monte Carlo Delivery Forecast
note: 10,000 futures are simulated by resampling weekly throughput from the chosen history window, each with its own seeded stream (common random numbers) so a slider nudges every future instead of re-drawing them and the histogram slides rather than jitters; futures pour in over ~1.4 s while the chance-of-hitting KPI and the 50/85/95 % lines converge, and dragging the target on the chart (role=slider, arrow keys) recolours the bars that make it and re-reads the odds from the same counts. Set --dbp-forecast-h to 100dvh in an app.
html:
FernwoodDelivery forecast
Method

Each simulated future draws every week's output at random from the chosen history window, then works through the backlog plus scope growth of between half and one-and-a-half times the stated rate; the finish day falls inside the last week in proportion to the work left. 10,000 futures make the distribution.

name: Cross-team Dependency Chord
note: A directed chord built by hand: each team's band is split into what it needs and what it provides, and every ribbon leaves the requesting team at full width and narrows to an arrow point in the provider, so direction reads without a legend. Status filters, request-vs-effort weighting and status edits re-run the layout and tween every start and end angle (new ribbons grow from zero width in place); ribbons multiply-blend on the paper ground, and the same requests drive a subgrid matrix and a sortable list. Set --dbp-deps-h to 100dvh in an app.
